newsitem.title: USA: CENTRAL ILLINOIS DRY AREAS GET LIGHT SHOWERS - WSC.
newsitem.headline: CENTRAL ILLINOIS DRY AREAS GET LIGHT SHOWERS - WSC.

text.p: The driest areas of central Illinois received just light showers Tuesday through early Wednesday, but central Indiana and western Ohio benefitted from rainfall of between 0.30 to 1.50 inches, said Weather Services Corp senior agricultural meteorologist Joel Burgio.
"That will stabilize the conditions of the corn and soybean crops in Indiana and Ohio. However, corn conditions are expected to decline in central Illinois," Burgio said.
He noted the western corn belt (Iowa, Minnesota and Nebraska) had very light showers on Tuesday with amounts of a trace to 0.05 inch.

During the past 24 hours, temperatures across the U.S. Midwest ranged from below normal in Iowa and Minnesota to near normal in southern Iillinois and Indiana. Highs were 66 to 74 degrees (Fahrenheit) in the western corn belt and 82 to 88 F in the eastern corn belt on Tuesday afternoon, Burgio said.
He expected showers to linger in the Ohio River Valley early Wednesday morning. Otherwise, fair weather was expected to prevail in the Midwest on Wednesday.
Friday's forecast called for showers to redevelop in parts of Nebraska and Iowa while Illinois and Indiana should see mostly fair conditions, Burgio said.

"During Friday, light showers will spread into Illinois and Indiana," Burgio said. "Between Thursday and Friday, rainfall will total between 0.10 and 0.50 inch with 50 to 60 percent coverage for parts of Iowa, Illinois and Indiana."
He predicted temperatures to average below normal during Wednesday and Thursday returning to near normal levels on Friday across the Midwest.

"Highs on Wednesday and Thursday will range between mid 70s to low 80s (F) and lows Wednesday night will range low 50s to middle 60s (F) with the coolest area being in Wisconsin and Michigan," Burgio said.
